title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We present preregistration, detailed execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), confirmatory analysis, representative diagnostic artifacts, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being investigated to translate high-level operator intent into device configuration sequences for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness requires that generated configurations satisfy deterministic invariants such as required ordering of multi-device operations, group-level safety constraints (e.g., at-least-one-up), access-control policies, and loop- or reachability-related properties. Prior work has produced prototype intent→config systems and proposed verifier-assisted repair architectures, but artifact-backed, preregistered empirical quantification of guarded generate→validate→repair pipelines in tightly controlled paired designs is limited [1],[2].

This study addresses the preregistered research question (CAND-2026-001): under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair increase the per-task probability that a deterministic verifier accepts the configuration? Because the design fixes shared_initial_candidate semantics, the estimand isolates the marginal effect of an automated verifier-triggered repair applied to an identical initial candidate (a repair-only effect); it does not estimate benefits from independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, multi-sample selection, or sampling-parameter tuning.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis reporting baseline acceptance 199/200 and guarded acceptance 200/200 with exact contingency counts and inferential quantities (McNemar p, paired-bootstrap CI). (4) A focused failure diagnosis for the single repaired pair using archived validator traces. (5) Reproducibility guidance and a bounded interpretation of operational implications grounded in the archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Intent-driven configuration synthesis and LLM-assisted NetOps are active research directions [1],[3],[4]. Several recent prototype systems evaluate intent→config accuracy on curated tasks or integrate emulators for limited end-to-end tests [1],[3]. Cross-domain generate→validate→repair patterns—especially in program repair and constrained synthesis—motivate guarded architectures where an external oracle or test-suite verifies candidate outputs and triggers bounded repair calls [5],[6]. Surveys and safety analyses in the agentic-LLM literature highlight hallucination/confabulation and recommend verifier gates, provenance, and conservative tool access in operational pipelines [7],[8].

Synthesis and gap. Many prior works either evaluate independent first-pass generation accuracy or present repair frameworks in software engineering; few provide a preregistered paired design that reuses the identical initial candidate to isolate the repair-only effect. The present artifact-grounded experiment directly targets this narrower empirical gap and therefore complements existing prototype and conceptual results without claiming broader production generality.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 before observing outcomes. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, defined as the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). Generation semantics were fixed to shared_initial_candidate; each task produced exactly one initial model generation deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes. The pipeline allowed at most one automatic repair call per task. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on discordant pairs; a paired-bootstrap (percentile) CI for the risk difference was also planned (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Task bank and selection. Tasks were created by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; the preregistration specified a deterministic index mapping to select 200 tasks from the adapter's challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (ordered atom-level operations), allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (group invariants, must-be-down preconditions). The manifest also stores a difficulty pattern label (very_hard or extreme), required_command_count, and changed_interface_count. Inclusion/exclusion rules (token-normalized leakage checks and syntactic pre-checks) were applied before model calls; the archived run recorded zero preregistered exclusions.

Model and sampling semantics. The declared model (execution/model_configuration.json) is gpt-5-mini. That file records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; the hosted-provider sampling nondeterminism is not eliminated by an unset temperature. The adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 imposed shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per task, reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Provider-call accounting in deterministic_reconciliation.json reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1.

Deterministic verifier and scoring. The oracle deterministic_netops_validator_v5 deterministically parses generated configurations, enforces allowed-field constraints, checks required_sequence ordering, validates group-level invariants (e.g., exactly_active constraints), and reports structured violation codes. The binary scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation returns 1 only when all encoded invariants pass; otherwise it returns 0 and emits a detailed validator_trace containing validation_before and validation_after snapshots. These per-episode validator traces and the shared-initial provider traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/.

Experimental semantics and missingness. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were used, any difference between baseline and guarded acceptance for a pair can occur only if the verifier-triggered repair modifies the initial candidate. The preregistered missingness plan treated persistent unparsable outputs as failures in a sensitivity analysis; in the archived execution no persistent unparsables occurred. The experiment completed all preregistered pairs (complete_pair_count = 200).

Statistical analysis. The confirmatory analysis used the exact two-sided McNemar implementation on discordant counts (n10 = guarded=1,before=0; n01 = guarded=0,baseline=1). For general reproducibility we report the exact calculation used by the executor: with discordant total n = n10 + n01 and observed k = n10, the two-sided p is computed as ptwo = 2 * min{BinomialCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomialCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)}. For our observed discordants (n = 1, k = 1) this yields p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile CIs for the risk difference were computed with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729) as recorded in analysis_log.jsonl. All analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/*.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, analysis_log.jsonl).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and reconciliation. The execution manifest records started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00, planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 201. Deterministic_reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent pair accounting. Provider-call audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 201, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation:200, repair:1}.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). analysis/condition_summary.csv contains the exact per-condition counts: baseline successes = 199, failures = 1 (success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200, failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) lists n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the observed discordant counts using the executor's binomial-calculation method. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference was [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All these numeric values exactly match archived analysis/results.json and the CSV artifacts.

Repair activity and diagnostic artifact. The guarded pipeline invoked a single automated repair (repair stage count = 1). The archived validator_trace for the repaired pair identifies the failure as a required_sequence (multi-step ordering) violation: the shared initial candidate violated an explicit ordered step in the task manifest (required_sequence length = 9 for that task; changed_interface_count = 3). The repair applied a small reordering patch that restored the required ordering and satisfied group invariants; post-repair the verifier returned valid = true. Representative artifacts for the repaired pair are archived (execution/responses/task-000008-*, execution/scoring/task-000008-*) and include parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, validation_before/after snapshots, and violation_codes. These artifacts permit a precise, auditable diagnosis of the repaired failure without human interpretation beyond reading the archived traces.

Missingness, exclusions, contamination. The run recorded no preregistered exclusions and no missing pairs: complete_pairs = 200 and baseline_only_observed_pairs = guarded_only_observed_pairs = both_missing_pairs = 0. contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged entries. The deterministic_reconciliation provider-call audit shows no cross-condition cache-key reuse and all deterministic consistency checks passed.

Exploratory diagnostics. The archived task manifests permit exploratory stratification by difficulty pattern, required_command_count, and changed_interface_count. In the archived sample the single failed baseline episode (the repaired case) occurred on an extreme/very_hard composite with required_command_count = 9 and changed_interface_count = 3, consistent with the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device ordering constraints concentrate failure risk. analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg visualizes per-condition rates and the bootstrap distribution used for CI construction; the figure artifact is archived and indexed by the execution manifest.
sections.discussion:
Estimand interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because baseline and guarded conditions began from the identical initial candidate for every task, the observed paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair on that identical candidate (a repair-only effect). This estimand does not capture benefits that could arise from alternative guarded designs (independently prompted guarded generations, constrained prompting, temperature modulation, or mult-sample selection); those are distinct interventions requiring separate preregistered contrasts.

Statistical regime and power considerations. The preregistration targeted detection of ~10–15 percentage-point paired improvements at N = 200 under baseline assumptions ≈45–65% success. The observed baseline rate (199/200 = 99.5%) substantially exceeded planning assumptions, producing low realized power to detect small absolute differences and placing inference into a discrete discordant-count regime. In such regimes the exact McNemar p-value can be noninformative for rare discordant outcomes (here p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair); the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] provides a useful bound on plausible effect sizes consistent with the data.

Operational implications and scope. The single repaired failure was a multi-device ordering breach that a single bounded repair corrected in this synthetic deterministic setting. This supports a constrained conclusion: in this controlled environment, a verifier-triggered repair can correct certain localized ordering faults on identical initial candidates. It does not imply that verifier-guarded repair will recover from semantic misinterpretations of intent, omissions only detectable via live dataplane telemetry, or adversarially poisoned context; those remain open empirical questions.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics and exactly one sampled generation per task limit conclusions strictly to repair effects applied to identical candidates. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants described in task manifests but does not emulate all live-device behaviors or dataplane telemetry; some operational failure modes require live execution/measurement. External validity: the experiment used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank; results do not establish multi-model generality or production-readiness. Conclusion validity: the very small number of discordant pairs yields large sampling uncertainty for small absolute effects; the bootstrap CI quantifies this uncertainty.

Reproducibility and archived artifacts. Reanalysis is reproducible using the archived bundle. Key artifacts and their authoritative accounting are indexed in the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json: execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 as recorded in execution manifest), execution/model_configuration.json (declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini; temperature = null), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (full task manifests), execution/provider_calls/* (provider traces), execution/scoring/* (validator traces), analysis/*.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (bootstrap seed and resample count). To reproduce the paired-bootstrap CI, run the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor on execution/raw_results.jsonl with bootstrap_seed = 1729 and bootstrap_resamples = 10000; these exact parameters are recorded in analysis_log.jsonl.

Recommended next steps (artifact-grounded). To increase operational relevance and address open questions indicated by the archived run, future preregistered studies should: (1) adopt independent first-pass generation semantics to measure the effect of constrained/guarded prompting separate from repair; (2) test multiple models to assess cross-model generality beyond gpt-5-mini; (3) expand task diversity and incorporate live-device emulation or dataplane verification to capture runtime behaviors beyond static invariants; and (4) include systematic adversarial contamination or poisoned-retrieval experiments. Each recommendation follows directly from limitations observed in the archived execution (single model, synthetic tasks, shared_initial_candidate semantics, limited adversarial testing).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In this synthetic deterministic task set using gpt-5-mini, baseline verifier acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with a paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); the exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a narrow conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All execution, provider, verifier, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived and indexed by the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json for reproducible reanalysis.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Provider-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
